newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA CUTS MAIN INTEREST RATE TO 8.03 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA CUTS MAIN INTEREST RATE TO 8.03 PCT.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Thursday it would cut its main interest rate to 8.03 percent monthly from 14.15 percent as yield of short-term government securities fell further this week.
The new interest rate goes in force on Monday.
"The BNB sets the main interest rate at 8.03 percent monthly from April 21, down from 14.15 percent now," the BNB said in a statement.
The rate cut reflected the falling yield of one-week discount T-bills auctioned by the Finance Ministry in the past week, a BNB official said.

The weighted average effective monthly yield of one-week discount T-bills auctioned by the Finance Ministry since Friday through Thursday fell to 8.03 percent from 14.15 percent the week before, BNB figures showed.

Next week the BNB would adjust the main rate to the yields of one-week and four-week discount T-bill issues auctioned daily to take into account the rising volume of four-week paper bought at the primary auctions recently, the statement said.

Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund the BNB adjusts the main rate weekly to the weighted average effective monthly yield of short-term government securities auctioned in five successive days by the Finance Ministry.
The International Monetary Fund has disbursed $178.7 million of the $657 million package which was approved by the IMF board last week, the BNB said.
Under the accord Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board, to restore confidence in its collapsing financial system.
Interest rates would be set by the market and are expected to decline gradually under the currency board mechanism.
The system would require levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank and preventing the printing of money.
Economists envisage long-term stabilisation of the financial system once the new government and parliament are formed after April 19 elections.
The caretaker government in office for the past two months has stabilised the lev from 2,800 levs per dollar in mid-February to around 1,500 now with monthly inflation in March at 12.3 percent.
Monthly inflation rate for April was expected to be below the March level, a National Statistics Institute expert said.
